name: Chouine
description: Chouine is a traditional French trick-taking card game played mainly in and around the Loire Valley. It is primarily a two-player game, though adaptations for 3 or 4 players exist. The game combines trick-taking with declarations of combinations (marianna) that determine trumps and score bonus points. An annual Chouine World Championship is held in Lavardin.

content.text: Chouine is a traditional French trick-taking card game played mainly in and around the Loire Valley. It is primarily a two-player game, though adaptations for 3 or 4 players exist. The game combines trick-taking with declarations of combinations (marianna) that determine trumps and score bonus points. An annual Chouine World Championship is held in Lavardin.

Country/Region of Origin: Loire Valley, France
Time Period: Origins said to date from 16th century, though modern form developed later
Historical Development: The game has enjoyed a revival in recent years, with formalized rules and organized play. Annual World Championship now held.
Cultural Significance: Traditional game of the Loire Valley region, now experiencing renewed interest.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 2
Partnerships: No (individual play)

Type: French-suited 32-card pack
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Cards: Ace, 10, King, Queen, Jack, 9, 8, 7 in each suit
Card Values: Ace=11, 10=10, King=4, Queen=3, Jack=2, 9/8/7=0

32-card French deck
Score sheet
Table space

Cards per Player: Varies (5 cards each in basic game)
Talon: Remaining cards form stock
Dealing Pattern: Alternating cards
First Dealer: Determined by drawing cards - lower rank deals
